<!-- pr-reviewer: 6acf142578af0cbe9feca978add337ad6428b858 -->
**Verdict: Needs changes before merge** (one real gap in the idle guarantee; everything else is sound). Reviewed the commits beyond #474's head c051ba9d (c33f8f9f, 6acf1425).

**What looks good**
- Idle clock resets only after a complete line has been answered (`active = Instant::now()` after `forward`, listen.rs ~L277), so app answering time does not count and partial bytes do not reset it.
- Drop is logged by peer name (`client <peer> dropped: idle - no complete line for Ns; serving the next client`), the client gets a `notifications/message` warning, and the accept loop serves the next client. Test covers this.
- `listen_with_idle` is configurable, `Inbox::listen` keeps the 5 min default, windows below POLL are clamped. No unwrap/panic added in src.
- #474 properties intact: non-JSON refusal, `MAX_LINE` bounded read, 5 s write timeout, stop/join. Tests use 300-400 ms windows, no long sleeps (suite 1.3 s).

**Local results (merged with upstream/main, clean merge, no conflicts)**
| check | result |
|---|---|
| `mcp_live` (app) | 9 passed |
| `mcp`, `mcp_pick`, `mcp_render`, `mcp_setup` | 13, 2, 5, 3 passed |
| `clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -D warnings` | clean |
| ui `mcp_live` | not run (no ui change beyond #474) |

**Requested before merge**
1. Slow-loris can still hold the session. The idle check is only at the top of the `serve_client` loop (listen.rs ~L249), but `read_until` (L262) does not return to it while bytes keep arriving: it only returns on newline, EOF, error, or a read timeout. A client trickling one byte every <50 ms (POLL) with no newline never lets a read time out, so the loop never re-checks `active.elapsed()`; it holds the session until the 16 MB cap (days at that rate). Partial bytes do not reset the clock, but the clock is never consulted. This is from reading the code, I did not run a trickle test. Fix: check the deadline inside the read (e.g. read with `fill_buf`/`read` into `buf` yourself and test `active.elapsed() >= idle` after every chunk, or set the socket read timeout to the remaining idle time), and add a test that trickles bytes faster than POLL and is dropped on schedule.

**Notes (not blocking)**
- The listen.rs doc/PR text says a partial line cannot hold the session; that is only true once item 1 is fixed.
- listen.rs is 336 lines, under the limit. Body has `Changelog:` and `Fixes #567`; no CHANGELOG.md or snapshot edits. Stacked on #474, so it can merge only after it.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 936954e77b76da7dd0a4f91e6ed6527f3b216dd4 -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge** (re-review at 936954e7; the slow-loris blocker from 6acf1425 is fixed).

**What looks good**
- `crates/app/src/mcp/listen.rs` `serve_client` no longer uses `read_until`. Each pass sets the socket read timeout to `min(remaining idle, POLL)` (floored at 1 ms) and reads at most `CHUNK` (8 KiB). The deadline is re-checked after every chunk, and a partial line never resets `active`. A client trickling bytes with no newline is now dropped on schedule.
- The #474 properties hold. The read is still capped by `MAX_LINE + 1` through the `room` clamp, with the oversize refusal and close kept after the loop. The write timeout is unchanged. Non-JSON input is still refused in `forward`. Several lines arriving in one chunk are forwarded in order.
- No `unwrap`, `expect` or `panic` in the new code. It uses `checked_sub`, `get`/`get_mut` and `saturating_add`.
- New test `a_trickling_client_is_dropped_on_the_idle_schedule`: it sends one `{` every 10 ms (poll step is 50 ms) with a 400 ms window. It asserts the idle note arrives between 350 ms and 1.5 s, that the log names the client address, and that the next client is served. It has a 5 s client read timeout and a bounded trickle thread, so a regression fails instead of hanging. The log capture is now shared once per binary.

**Local results (merged with upstream/main; clean merge)**
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test mcp_live` | 10 passed, 0 failed (1.3 s, no long sleeps) |
| `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test mcp` | 13 passed, 0 failed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

**Requested before merge**
None.

**Notes (not blocking)**
- `listen.rs` is 360 lines, under the ~400 limit.
- I ran only the delta-related suites (mcp_live, mcp) and clippy, not the ui suite, because the delta touches no ui code.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
